prompt:
What volume of $0.200\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$ HCl(aq) exactly neutralises $25.0\ \text{cm}^3$ of $0.100\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$ Na$_2$CO$_3$(aq)?

Na$_2$CO$_3$(aq) + 2HCl(aq) → 2NaCl(aq) + H$_2$O(l) + CO$_2$(g)
0.10 mol of magnesium is added to 0.10 mol of HCl. Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. What amount of hydrogen forms?
markscheme: **A.** HCl is limiting (0.10/2 = 0.05 < 0.10/1); 0.10 mol HCl gives 0.050 mol H₂.

prompt: Which type of reaction always has an atom economy of 100%?
markscheme: **B.** All the reactant atoms end up in the single product.

prompt:
Aspirin (M = 180.17 g mol⁻¹) is made from salicylic acid (M = 138.13 g mol⁻¹) in a 1 : 1 reaction with excess ethanoic anhydride.

**(a)** Calculate the theoretical yield of aspirin from 2.76 g of salicylic acid. **[2]**

**(b)** 2.88 g of aspirin is obtained. Calculate the percentage yield. **[1]**

**(c)** Suggest two reasons why the yield is less than 100%. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $n = 2.76/138.13 = 0.0200\ \text{mol}$ ✓; $m = 0.0200\times180.17 = 3.60\ \text{g}$ ✓

**(b)** $2.88/3.60\times100 = 80.0\%$ ✓

**(c)** Any two: incomplete reaction; side reactions; loss of product during filtration/transfer/recrystallisation; product left dissolved in solvent ✓✓
